result_text:
I fixed the four broken default scoping conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`, and I added a regression test. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes offline (107 test classes, no failures or errors), and the new test passes (8 cases).

Changes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **HTML generator rules** (pkgdown, Doxygen, `<meta name="generator">`): the path pattern `.*[.](html|html|xhtml)` is now `.*[.](html?|xhtml)`, so `.htm` matches and `.html` and `.xhtml` still do.
- **.NET documentation XML**: `.*/[.]xml` is now `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches.
- **`// Generated by …` JavaScript**: `.*/[.]js` is now `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches.
- **Gradle JavaScript scripts**: `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` is now `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

The new test is `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It checks that the `.htm` pkgdown, Doxygen and meta-generator pages land in the generated scope, that a `<doc>` XML file and a `// Generated by` JS file do too, and that `build-gradle.js` lands in build-and-deployment. It also checks that hand-written `.htm`, `.xml` and `.js` files stay out, and that `.html`, `.xhtml` and `build.gradle` still match.

Nothing is committed.
